questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A: When you squeeze one end of a tube to get toothpaste out from the other end, Pascal’s principle is observed.

Reason R: A change in the pressure applied to an enclosed incompressible fluid is transmitted undiminished to every portion of the fluid and to the walls of its container.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is not correct but R is correct
A is correct but R is not correct
Both A and R is correct and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Pascal's law states that the pressure in a closed incompressible fluid is transmitted equally in all directions.

The formula for pressure is given by

P=FA

When a toothpaste is squeezed let the pressure transmitted by P. At the mouth of the toothpaste the pressure will also be equal to P due to Pascal's law. The pressure applied to the tube is transmitted equally throughout the toothpaste. When the pressure reaches the open end, it forces toothpaste out through the opening. Hence, both A&R is correct and R is correct explanation for  A.

Volume of water flowing out=Av, where A is area of opening and v is speed of water from the opening.

questions.q:

Assertion (A): Clothes containing oil or grease stains cannot be cleaned by water wash.

Reason (R) : Because the angle of contact between the oil/ grease and water is obtuse. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the option given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Angle of contact between oil and water is obtuse i.e., greater than critical angle of contact θc>90°, therefore they do not stick and that's the reason grease/oil stains can not be removed by water wash. 

Thus, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

The force exerted on the vertical wall just in front of the tube which stops water horizontally flowing out of the tube, is: [given : density of water <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1000</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

questions.solution:
Volume of water coming out of the pipe per sec =Av=10×10-4×20=0.02 m3 s-1

Mass of water hitting the wall per second m=0.02×103=20 kg s-1

As the water hits the wall normal to the wall and stops, the change of momentum of water hitting the wall is =m0--v=mv

=20×20=400 kg m s-2

Since, the change of momentum obtained is per unit time, it is same as the force.  

Thus, the force acting on the wall by water = force experienced by water jet=400 N.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : If a capillary tube is immersed first in cold water and then in hot water, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in hot water.
Statement II : If a capillary tube is immersed first in cold water and then in hot water, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in cold water.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For water, the surface tension decreases as the temperature increases. At higher temperatures, the water molecules have more kinetic energy and are better able to overcome the cohesive forces at the surface, resulting in a decrease in surface tension.

So, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in hot water and larger in cold water.

Hence, statement I is true, but statement II is false.

questions.q:
A 400 g solid cube having an edge of length 10 cm floats in water. How much volume of the cube is outside the water ?
(Given : density of water $=1000 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Volume of cube inside water
$\begin{aligned}
& =\left(\frac{\text { Denslty of cube }}{\text { Denslty of water }}\right) \times \text { Volume of cube } \\
& =\frac{\text { Mass of cube }}{\text { Denslty of water }} \\
& =\frac{400 \mathrm{gm}}{1 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{cm}^3} \\
& =400 \mathrm{~cm}^3
\end{aligned}$
Volume of cube outside water
$\begin{aligned}
& =\text { Volume of cube }- \text { Volume of cube inside water } \\
& =1000 \mathrm{~cm}^3-400 \mathrm{~cm}^3 \\
& =600 \mathrm{~cm}^3
\end{aligned}$

Assuming there is no atmospheric pressure on piston, P1=FπR2 and P2=P0.

⇒FπR2+ρgh1-h2=P0+12ρv22

⇒v2=2FπR2ρ-2P0ρ+2gh1-h2

v2=2×5×1053.14×12×1000-2×1.01×1051000+2×10×10

≈17.8 m s-1

questions.q: An ideal fluid of density 800 kg m-3, flows smoothly through a bent pipe (as shown in figure) that tapers in cross-sectional area from a to a2. From equation of continuity,

av1=a2v2⇒v2=2v1

From Bernoulli's theorem,

P1+12ρv12+ρgh1=P2+12ρv22+ρgh2⇒P1-P2=ρgh2-h1+12v22-v12⇒4100=80010-1+123v12⇒4100800+10=32v12⇒v1=1214×3=3636 m s-1

Therefore, x=363.

questions.q: A plane is in level flight at constant speed and each of its two wings has an area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>.</mo></math> If the speed of the air is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>180</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> over the lower wing surface and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>252</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> over the upper wing surface, the mass of the plane is ________<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kg</mi><mo>.</mo></math> (Take air density to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
